extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when an examiner may require restriction/election, how to analyze independent/distinct species and burden, and how applicants must respond (including traversal, provisional election, and divisional strategy). Applies to US patent prosecution and notes PCT national-stage differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Election
rubrics_metrics.description: Election is the designation by applicant of the one of two or more inventions or patentably distinct species, or of the group of patentably indistinct species, that will be prosecuted in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Election identifies which invention/species (or grouping of indistinct species) the examiner will examine in the current application; other inventions/species may be pursued separately (e.g., via divisionals).

rubrics_metrics.name: When a Restriction Requirement May Be Made
rubrics_metrics.description: When two or more independent and distinct inventions are presented for examination, the examiner may make a restriction requirement if a serious search and/or examination burden exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner's authority to require restriction arises only when multiple independent/distinct inventions are claimed and continuation without restriction would impose a serious search/examination burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable Difference Requirement for Permissible Restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement for restriction is permissible if there is a patentable difference between the species/inventions as claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of patentable differences between claimed species or inventions supports separate treatment; identical or patentably indistinct claims weigh against restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serious Search and/or Examination Burden Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement for restriction is permissible if there would be a serious search and/or examination burden on the examiner if restriction is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when claims are separate, a restriction is only proper if the combined claims impose a significant burden on searching or examining that justifies dividing the claims into separate prosecution paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-Step Test for Restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should apply a two-step test: (1) independent or distinct — are the inventions independent (no relation) or distinct (related but separately patentable)? and (2) burden — is there a serious examination/search burden?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both prongs must be considered: first determine whether claims define independent or distinct inventions; then determine whether examining them together would create a substantial burden that warrants restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent Versus Distinct Inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent = no relation between the inventions; distinct = related but separately patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction informs whether claims can be grouped for examination: independent inventions are clearly separate, while distinct inventions may be related yet still patentably separable and thus potentially restricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of Species (as a Form of Restriction)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Election of Species requirement is a type of restriction requirement where the examiner asks the applicant to choose a single species or a single grouping of patentably indistinct species for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Election of species typically arises when multiple embodiments (species) of the same invention are claimed; the applicant must designate which embodiment(s) will be examined in the present application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Reply to a Restriction Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In the reply to the restriction requirement, applicant must elect one invention/species for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant's response must include a clear election; failure to elect may prevent examination progress. The election directs the examiner which claims to examine in the current file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traversal to Preserve Petition Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may traverse the restriction requirement with specific reasons why restriction is in error; a traversal is needed to preserve the right to petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To retain the ability to seek review of the restriction, the traversal must state particularized reasons contesting the restriction (general disagreement is insufficient). Filing a traversal preserves the applicant's right to subsequently petition the restriction requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Divisional Applications for Non-Elected Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-elected claims can be pursued in divisional applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims not elected for examination in the parent application may be prosecuted later by filing one or more divisional applications directed to those non-elected claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 121 Safe Harbor for Divisionals
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 121 safe harbor protects divisionals from double patenting if elected as a result of restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claims are elected as a result of a proper restriction, later-filed divisionals may be protected under § 121 from obviousness-type double patenting rejections arising from the parent application; this is an important strategic consideration when electing claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional Election Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional election allows examination to proceed while preserving the right to traverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may make a provisional election to enable prompt examination of chosen claims without waiving the right to contest the restriction; this can be used to delay deciding whether to traverse while keeping prosecution moving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone Restriction Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Telephone restriction practice can speed up resolution of restriction/election matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner-applicant telephone conferences regarding restriction/election issues may expedite clarification and resolution of restriction requirements and elections, helping to reduce delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT/National-Stage Unity of Invention Differences
rubrics_metrics.description: US restriction practice differs from the international PCT 'unity of invention' standard; for PCT national stage applications, the USPTO applies a unity of invention analysis (MPEP 1893.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that national-stage practice before the USPTO involves applying the PCT unity standard for PCT-derived filings, which can lead to different restriction/election outcomes than regular US practice; see MPEP 1893.03 for details.
